nonClaims: Nothing here says the platform or a tenant complies with any regulator text. The two sources are supervisory good practice and sound practice, not law.

Each row names a candidate carrier at harness and module level. carrierCheck NOT_CHECKED means no contract field or schema was read for this draft; R00 confirms or corrects each carrier before publication.
No evidence state is claimed. Every release-evidence cell at 19b176be is BLOCKED, NOT_RUN or NOT_SELECTED (0 QUALIFIED).
Practices are paraphrased, not quoted. Locators point to the held texts.
Gap kind TENANT_OBLIGATION names who implements a practice, never who bears the legal duty. Article 50(1) and 50(2) are written as duties on providers.
Whether any EU duty applies to the product today is not settled here: nothing is deployed and no jurisdiction is named.

rows.practice: Board and senior management align AI adoption and governance with business model, risk appetite and strategy.

gap.note: A board duty. The product can only supply records the tenant's board reads; the tenantAcceptance column is where the tenant records it.

rows.practice: Clear roles and responsibilities and an appropriate governance framework for AI adoption.

gap.note: H14 can hold an accountable owner per agent and approval routes; naming the people and their roles stays with the tenant.

rows.practice: Risk management frameworks that address AI risks, including documentation of AI use and materiality and risk assessment.

gap.note: The registry documents AI use; the risk framework itself is the tenant's.

rows.practice: Learn, adapt and adjust oversight, governance, risk practices and capabilities as AI evolves.

gap.note: An organisational capability. No product contract carries it.

rows.practice: A systematic way to assess the materiality and risk of each AI use case at inception and afterwards.

gap.note: Not checked: whether a published H14 contract carries a materiality or risk tier per use case, and a re-assessment trigger.

rows.practice: Select AI models or systems against business objectives, operational and technical needs, and use-case materiality and risk.

gap.note: The release profile pins the provider set; the selection decision and its rationale are the tenant's.

rows.practice: Data governance that keeps data fit for purpose (accurate, complete, consistent, reliable, secure) for training, testing and use.

gap.note: The banking pack's data-readiness assessment (IND-BANK-002) checks declared data classes and readiness; the banking pack is not in the release set yet (release-profile nonClaims), so the industry-pack row is the white-goods pack.

rows.practice: Understand explainability differences, prefer more explainable AI or add compensating controls, and give transparency fitted to each stakeholder.

gap.note: Traces and retrieval citations give technical explanation; stakeholder-tailored transparency (customer, staff, supervisor views) has no named contract.

rows.practice: Evaluate AI performance in proportion to materiality and risk: performance assessment, testing and ongoing monitoring.

gap.note: Every part of the practice has a named carrier; MAPPED waits for R00's field-level confirmation (F-RA-1).

rows.practice: Human oversight fitted to each use case's materiality, risk, autonomy, complexity and explainability.

gap.note: Approval steps in orchestration are the likely carrier; not checked whether the oversight mode is set per use case by risk tier.

rows.practice: Manage AI-related cyber and ICT risks, including AI scenarios in tests and exercises.

gap.note: Every part of the practice has a named carrier; MAPPED waits for R00's field-level confirmation (F-RA-1).

rows.practice: Manage third-party AI dependency risk: performance, transparency, data quality, supply chain, concentration and business continuity.

gap.note: Pinned digests and a signed catalog cover supply chain; concentration and exit planning are the tenant's.

rows.practice: For agents, inventory attributes beyond models: agent identifiers, accessible tools, components, guardrails; where mature, certified status and permitted scope per agent.

gap.note: Not checked: whether the registry contract has tool-access, guardrail, certified-status and permitted-scope fields. DESIGN-UX-001's agent inventory view reads the same attributes; the two drafts should cite each other.

rows.practice: Break an agent's goal into steps with a control at each step that, if not met, blocks the next step.

gap.note: Every part of the practice has a named carrier; MAPPED waits for R00's field-level confirmation (F-RA-1).

rows.practice: Set a risk-based frequency and operating model for oversight, with triggers to move between oversight forms on performance metrics or user request.

gap.note: No named contract turns a metric threshold into an oversight-mode change.

rows.practice: Monitor agents continuously (AI may monitor AI, with its own evaluation) and record anomalies that may show misuse or scope creep, such as data access beyond the goal.

gap.note: Telemetry and policy decisions exist as carriers; a scope-creep detector (access beyond the certified scope) is not named.

rows.practice: Agents produce summaries of their actions and reasoning, cross-checked against other sources where appropriate.

gap.note: Decision-point logging is the likely carrier; not checked whether an action summary is a contract output and whether it is reconciled with the trace.

rows.practice: Red-team agents on recognising problems, avoiding repeated errors, escalating, stopping safely, handing over and returning to a safe state.

gap.note: No agent red-team campaign (including agent-to-agent) is named among the evidence producers at 19b176be.

rows.locator: SP10 oversight forms pdfPage 55; agentic list pdfPage 57
rows.practice: Risk-based, tested kill switch: pause, limit, override or remove an agent's access to systems, tools, data or decisions, from full stop to graduated degradation towards human operation.

gap.note: Policy deny and operator scale-down could carry a full stop; no contract is named for per-agent pause or graduated degradation, nor a test of it.
gap.itemState: BLOCKED; no item owns a tested per-agent pause with graduated degradation (roadmap, 2026-11-22)

rows.practice: Resilience planning and testing for agents covers fallback processes, recovery expectations and escalation routes.

gap.note: Product recovery is in the deploymentRecovery domain; business fallback processes are the tenant's.

rows.practice: Define consumer need and target market before designing and deploying AI-supported products.

gap.note: A product-governance duty of the firm.

rows.practice: Test consumer outcomes across consumer characteristics and scenarios.

gap.note: CONF-BANK-001's cohorts are the planned carrier; not yet published.

rows.practice: Proportionate controls for bias and accuracy, and decisions that can be explained.

gap.note: No bias evaluation is named among the evidence producers.

rows.practice: Tell consumers how AI is used and its limits, and test their understanding where appropriate.

gap.note: The disclosure journeys are DESIGN-UX-001's last open step; nothing carries them yet. Same carrier as EU-AIA-ART50-1-5.

rows.practice: Monitor live outcomes to spot and deal with issues quickly.

gap.note: Technical telemetry is carried; consumer-outcome metrics are not named (FCA 3.2 lists metric-only monitoring as an area for improvement).
gap.itemState: no item; the value table's metrics are the nearest (roadmap, 2026-11-22)

rows.practice: Proportionate, risk-based AI governance throughout the lifecycle.

gap.note: H14 carries lifecycle records; proportionality decisions are the firm's.

rows.practice: Clearly designed human oversight and escalation triggers, including thresholds for low confidence or uncertainty.

gap.note: Not checked whether an escalation threshold is a contract field.

rows.practice: Multidisciplinary governance backed by continuous monitoring: thresholds, dashboards, drift checks, logging and audit trails of AI interactions.

gap.note: Every part of the practice has a named carrier; MAPPED waits for R00's field-level confirmation (F-RA-1).

rows.practice: Senior managers accountable for AI systems and for reasonable steps to mitigate risk.

gap.note: An SMF duty of the firm.

rows.practice: Register agents in a central inventory: which are live, who owns them, what systems and data they reach, which controls apply.

gap.note: Same carrier and check as FSB-AG01.

rows.practice: Turn risk appetite into thresholds (for example red, amber, green) with predefined actions and escalation.

gap.note: Same gap as FSB-AG03: no contract binds a threshold to a predefined action.

rows.practice: AI systems and architecture that match the sensitivity and security needs of the use case.

gap.note: Every part of the practice has a named carrier; MAPPED waits for R00's field-level confirmation (F-RA-1).

rows.practice: AI model dependencies, including third-party ones, are part of operational resilience planning.

gap.note: The release profile lists the model provider and tenant facts; resilience mapping of business services is the firm's.

rows.practice: Mitigate cyber threats and over-dependence on one AI model or provider, with a way to switch.

gap.note: The release set has one model provider; a tested provider switch is not evidenced.

rows.practice: Manage third parties proactively: visibility of model changes, contingency and exit plans, tested vendor assurances.

gap.note: Digest pins make model changes visible; contracts, exit plans and vendor testing are the firm's.

gap.note: No disclosure journey is carried yet. The notice must not rely on colour alone and must be announced to a screen reader (50(5) accessibility). Showing it again after a reconnect, and to bank staff, are design choices beyond the text. Release condition (the visionary's read, a note on the release path at lock 78): no release to a tenant in the European Union without the disclosure journey. The product is deployed nowhere today. A planning reading, not legal advice.

rules: state MAPPED requires carrierCheck CONFIRMED or CORRECTED.
a row with candidateState MAPPED has state PARTIAL, gap kind CARRIER_UNCONFIRMED and carrierCheck NOT_CHECKED.
every non-MAPPED row carries a gap with a kind from the enum and a note.
every PRODUCT_GAP gap names carryingItems (roadmap ids) or, when the list is empty, noCarryingItem with the enum's one value.
every EU row carries dateAsEnacted and dateAsAmended; each date object cites a source and a confirmation.
a date object whose source has a held digest carries confirmation HELD_SOURCE and a locator; one whose source has none carries UNCONFIRMED.
dateAlreadyPassed is computed from dateAsEnacted against draftDate.
an obligationLocator naming two places gives a pdfPage for each place.

gapKindMeaning.PRODUCT_GAP: nothing in the product carries the practice yet
gapKindMeaning.TENANT_OBLIGATION: the tenant implements it in its own channel or organisation; this says nothing about who bears a legal duty
